subject: Pilot success map, success metrics & immediate access steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fluxwave.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@fluxwave.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot success map, success metrics & immediate access steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from Redwood's side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before kicking off the pilot. I tried to keep this tight with owners and dates.

High-level goal (what success looks like)
- Reduce average inference latency for your conversational agent from ~420ms to <= 180ms for 90th percentile while maintaining answer fidelity on the support prompt set.
- Achieve 30% token-cost reduction via batching + prefix caching by pilot end.

Scope (what we'll test in the 4-week pilot)
1) Model variant: run your current finetuned Llama-3-7B vs Redwood-optimized quantized Llama-3-7B-4bit and a latency-first variant (int8 pipeline).
2) Traffic profile: synthetic replay of 5k weekly QA queries + 10% live routing from staging.
3) Eval sets: "support-30" (customer-facing tickets), "kb-10" (internal knowledge checks), and randomized 50-shot prompt sampling.

Success metrics (primary + observability)
- Primary: 90p latency (ms), tokens-per-request cost (USD), and generation quality on support-30 (F1 + qualitative pass rate).
- Secondary: cold-start (first-token) latency, KV-cache hit rate, and error/retry count.

Owners & roles
- Redwood: Olga (pilot owner), Connor (infra + access), Diego (evaluation + prompt instrumentation)
- FluxWave: Samir (product lead), Priya (engineering lead)

Immediate asks from FluxWave (by Tue 21 Jul EOD)
- Provide a service account for s3 read (prefix: fluxwave/pilot-staging/) and a short-lived SSH key for staging VM access.
- Export of 1k representative support tickets (anonymized) + mapping file for intent classification.

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): access grant + dataset handoff + confirm eval prompts
- Week 1: baseline runs and metric collection (models A/B)
- Week 2: performance tuning (batching, cache policies), start live 10% routing
- Week 3: stability checks, quality regressions, and canary expansion
- Week 4: wrap, recommendation doc, and optional extension/commit conversation

Attachments enclosed: pilot-success-metrics-template.xlsx (baseline targets + data schema) and access-checklist.txt (S3 + IAM steps).

Next meeting: propose Thu 23 Jul 10:00am PT — 30 minutes for alignment and any final access items.

If anything here doesn't match your expectations, flag it and I'll update.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

From: Samir Khan <samir@fluxwave.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@fluxwave.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 16:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot success map, success metrics & immediate access steps

Thanks Olga — solid write-up. Quick answers and a couple clarifications below.

Access and data
- We've spun up an S3 staging bucket (s3://fluxwave-pilot-staging). I'll send a temporary IAM role via our infra ticketing system (ticket #INF-9821). Role grants read to fluxwave/pilot-staging/* for 14 days.
- Priya will drop the anonymized 1k ticket export into /ingest/support-1k.jsonl (schema matches your template). Expect that by Mon 21 Jul 12:00pm PT.

Model variants
- We can export your requested finetuned Llama-3-7B checkpoints to the staging bucket. Confirm preferred artifact naming convention (we prefer redwood-friendly names).

One ask from our side
- Can Redwood include a quick smoke test that logs request IDs so we can correlate traces in our Splunk instance? That will help our SRE validate end-to-end routing.

Scheduling
- Thu 23 Jul 10:00am PT works for us. We'll invite our SRE and a PM.

Samir
Product Lead, FluxWave
samir@fluxwave.ai

Great, Samir — I'll own the infra onboarding. Quick checklist and what I'll do next: 

Connor action items (this week)
- Create temporary assume-role policy and upload ARN to INF-9821 (expect by Mon 20 Jul 11:30am PT).
- Prepare a smoke-test script (bash + curl) that attaches an x-request-id header and emits a minimal JSON result — we'll commit to the staging repo at: https://git.redwood.com/fluxwave/pilot-smoke.
- Stand up a small canary env with batch-size tuning flags so we can compare token cost across 1/4/8/16 batch settings across model variants.

Notes for Diego / evaluation hooks
- Diego: I'll add a CloudWatch log group and grant you read access. Please add instrumentation in the eval harness to pull 90p latency and KV-cache hit rate. Use tag key "pilot:fluxwave-2026".

Attachments referenced: access-checklist.txt (contains the S3 prefix and SSH key instructions).

I'll update INF-9821 when role is ready and post the smoke test link to the pilot doc.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien

1) Eval prompt set: Diego will upload the "support-30" and "kb-10" prompt manifests to the Google doc (link below) by Tue EOD. If you want to flag any prompts to exclude, add a comment directly in the doc.

2) Governance / security: Samir, if you can forward the minimal DLP checklist (PII redaction rules) we will confirm that the export matches. We will not persist raw ticket text in production — only in the isolated staging bucket used for evaluation.

I'll also attach the filled pilot-success-metrics-template.xlsx after we have week-1 baseline numbers.
